SYNTHETIC FIXTURE: casual human-styled text for tests. Not real content.
I finally fixed the gate on Saturday. It had been sagging for about two years, ever since the big storm took out the post on the left, and every time I walked the dog I had to lift it with my knee just to get the latch to catch. My neighbor Dale told me it'd take twenty minutes. It took most of the afternoon. First I had to find the post hole digger, which was not in the shed where I swore I'd left it but behind the water heater in the basement, under a pile of old paint cans. Then the ground was harder than I expected. Clay. Dug maybe eight inches before I hit a rock the size of a bowling ball and spent half an hour levering it out with a crowbar while the dog watched from the porch like I was an idiot, which, fair. My back hurt by two o'clock. Around then Dale wandered over with two beers and no offer to help, and we stood there arguing about whether concrete or gravel was better for the footing. He said gravel drains better. I said concrete doesn't wiggle. We both used the word "obviously" a lot. In the end I mixed a bag of quick-set, poured it in around a fresh four-by-four, and checked it with the little yellow level about nine times. The bubble kept drifting left. Eventually I stopped caring. By dinner the gate swung shut on its own with a satisfying clunk, and the latch caught the first try. Then it rained, naturally. Sunday morning the post hadn't moved. Small win, but I'll take it, and I'm still a little proud of that clunk every time I come home. The dog, for the record, has not once thanked me. She just walks through it now like it was always that easy, tail going, never looking back at the post.
